Когда ответ готов, напиши его последней строкой в формате FINAL: <ответ>.
Формат ответа в FINAL: только сама сущность — имя, число, название, место или дата, не длиннее пяти слов. На языке вопроса.
Не добавляй ничего, о чём не спросили напрямую: к дате не приписывай год, если вопрос не просит именно год; к городу не приписывай страну или регион; не оборачивай ответ в предложение и не поясняй его.
Пример: если вопрос про дату события — FINAL: 15 September, а не FINAL: 15 September, 2026. Если вопрос про место — FINAL: New Delhi, а не FINAL: New Delhi, India.
Для числовых задач в FINAL только число.

The first areas of England met heatwave conditions during the morning of 6 July as temperatures in parts of south-eastern England exceeded 28 °C (82 °F) for the third consecutive day; temperatures that day peaked at 34.0 °C (93.2 °F) in Teddington. The following day more areas met heatwave criteria, although peak temperatures decreased with a maximum of 32.4 °C (90.3 °F) recorded at both Frittenden and Teddington. On 8 July, temperatures peaked at 33.8 °C (92.8 °F) at Heathrow Airport, whilst Wales saw a peak of 31.2 °C (88.2 °F) at Bute Park, Scotland a peak of 29.0 °C (84.2 °F) at Aboyne, and Northern Ireland a peak of 27.1 °C (80.8 °F) at Helen's Bay. The Met Office warned of an "extreme" marine heatwave affecting parts of the English Channel and North Sea that could be detrimental to some marine life including seagrasses and shellfish, with sea temperatures reaching 4–5 °C (7.2–9.0 °F) above average. On 9 July, temperatures peaked at 35.5 °C (95.9 °F) in Wisley, making it the eighth day of the year when temperatures exceeded 34 °C (93 °F), breaking the previous record of seven set in 1976 and equalled in 2020. The highest temperature recorded in Wales was 31.3 °C (88.3 °F) at Bute Park, as Scotland saw highs of 29.3 °C (84.7 °F) at Charterhall and Northern Ireland reached 27.5 °C (81.5 °F) at Killowen. Five locations experienced a tropical night, with a minimum temperature of 21.3 °C (70.3 °F) reported at Heathrow.

The first areas of the country met heatwave conditions on 24 May, when temperature thresholds were reached in eight locations in Essex, London, Oxfordshire and Suffolk. England, Wales and all recorded their highest temperatures of the year so far at 32.3 °C (90.1 °F) in Kew Gardens, 27.4 °C (81.3 °F) in Cardiff and 23.4 °C (74.1 °F) in Armagh; Scotland reached 23.5 °C (74.3 °F) in Edinburgh, just short of a high recorded earlier in May. Jersey's record for the hottest May day ever was broken as temperatures reached 29.2 °C (84.6 °F) in St Helier, breaking the previous record of 28.9 °C (84.0 °F) set in 2003.
On 21 June, the first areas of the country met heatwave conditions as temperatures surpassed 27 °C (81 °F) for the third consecutive day in Writtle, with temperatures peaking at 31.8 °C (89.2 °F) at Heathrow Airport. The following day the highest temperature was 32.5 °C (90.5 °F), recorded in Yeovilton. Thunderstorms across parts of southern England that evening prompted a yellow weather warning, with flash flooding, power cuts, travel disruption and several house fires caused by the storms, including one in Bristol that forced the evacuation of multiple homes.
Many parts of the country experienced a tropical night, with the Welsh record for highest minimum June temperature broken in St Athan when readings did not fall below 20.3 °C (68.5 °F). On 23 June, temperatures peaked at 34.6 °C (94.3 °F) in Wisley, with 32.3 °C (90.1 °F) recorded in Wales as both Scotland and Northern Ireland saw their hottest days of the year so far at 29.0 °C (84.2 °F) in Dyce and 28.1 °C (82.6 °F) in Katesbridge. More areas experienced another tropical night, with the highest overnight low of 22.3 °C (72.1 °F) recorded at RAF Brize Norton. The record for the hottest June day in the United Kingdom was broken on 24 June after 36.1 °C (97.0 °F) was recorded in Gosport, surpassing the previous record of 35.6 °C (96.1 °F) set in 1957 and equalled in 1976.
